chapterThermodynamics high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on identifying the adiabatic curve on a P-V diagram by comparing slopes of adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric processes, which is thermodynamics.
subtopic 1Adiabatic Process
subtopic 2not assigned (one subtopic chosen)
why this subtopicThe answer depends on the adiabatic curve on a P-V diagram being steeper than the isothermal curve (slope -gamma P/V versus -P/V), a property of the adiabatic process.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below. Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is
  1. 1
  2. 2
  3. 3
  4. 4
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
  1. (dPdV)adiabatic = -γ P
  2. (dPdV)isothermal = -P
  3. (dPdV)adiabatic > (dPdV)isothermal

→ the working concludes: unclear

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · high
  1. Curve 1 is vertical (V constant), so it is isochoric.
  2. Curve 4 is horizontal (P constant), so it is isobaric.
  3. For the isothermal process PV = const, so dPdV = -PV.
  4. For the adiabatic process PVγ = const, so dPdV = -γPV.
  5. Since γ > 1, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal one from the same initial state.
  6. Curve 2 is steeper than curve 3, so curve 2 is adiabatic, which is option 2.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
22 highagree
difficultymedium · 2 steps
stepsEliminate the straight lines: the vertical line (constant V) is isochoric and the horizontal line (constant P) is isobaric, leaving the two curves → Recall that the adiabatic slope dP/dV = -γ P/V is γ times the isothermal slope -P/V, so the adiabatic is the steeper of the two curves from the common initial point and pick that curve
why it is trickyThe work is identifying the isochoric and isobaric lines by sight, then using the γ-times-steeper slope relation to tell the adiabatic curve from the isothermal one.

ConceptOn a P-V diagram the adiabatic and the isothermal both fall, and the adiabatic is the steeper of the two because its slope carries the extra factor γ

NoteThe figure was supplied to this step as a drawn spec and could be read: from the common initial point, curve 4 is the horizontal line, curve 1 the vertical line, and curves 3 and 2 both fall with 2 the steeper, which is consistent with the key of 2.
What catches a student
The trapoption 3Reversedreversedthe right thing stated backwards: direction, order or ratio

Two of the four curves fall as the volume rises and only their steepness separates them, so holding the adiabatic to be the gentler of the two picks curve 3, the isothermal.

Who fallsa student who knows the adiabatic and the isothermal are the two curved processes but carries the steepness comparison between them the wrong way round

Why it feels rightcurve 3 is a smooth decaying curve with no heat flow visibly attached to it, and nothing on the figure labels which of the two curves is which

  1. okThe flat line is isobaric and the vertical line isochoric, so the adiabatic must be one of the two falling curves.
  2. badAn adiabatic change is the gentler of the two, so it is curve 3.At the same point the adiabatic slope is γ times the isothermal slope and γ > 1, so the adiabatic falls faster -- the steeper curve, 2.
Also pullsoption 1

Who fallsa student who reads adiabatic as meaning nothing is exchanged with the surroundings at all, including work

Why it feels rightthe vertical line is the one process in which the gas visibly does nothing to its container, which matches a process sealed off from its surroundings

  1. okIn an adiabatic process no heat crosses the boundary.
  2. badSo nothing is exchanged and the volume cannot change; the process is the vertical curve 1.An adiabatic change still does work, paid for out of internal energy, so the volume does change; the vertical line at constant volume is the isochoric process the stem also lists.
No route to itoption 4

read the figure's geometry: this curve is the horizontal line from the initial state, so P is constant along it, which is the isobaric process the stem itself names among the four; every adiabatic relation for an ideal gas, PVγ or TVγ-1 constant, requires P to fall as V rises, so no reading of the adiabatic condition produces a flat line

The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration in rad/s2 is
  1. 2π
  2. 4π
  3. 12π
  4. 104π
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
  1. Angular acceleration α = ωf - ωit
  2. ωf = 3120 × 2π60 rad/s
  3. ωi = 1200 × 2π60 rad/s
  4. ⇒ α = (3120 - 1200)16 × 2π60 = 4π

→ the working concludes: option 2

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · high
  1. Change in angular speed: Δ n = 3120 - 1200 = 1920 rpm.
  2. Convert to rev/s: 192060 = 32 rev/s.
  3. Convert to rad/s: Δω = 2π × 32 = 64π rad/s.
  4. α = Δωt = 64π16 = 4π rad/s2, which is option 2.

chapterSemiconductor Electronics high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on the forward/reverse bias behaviour of p-n junction diodes in each circuit, which is semiconductor electronics.
subtopic 1PN Junction Diode Under Forward Bias
subtopic 2PN Junction Diode Under Reverse Bias
why subtopic 1The answer depends on recognising that the two series diodes are both identically biased in circuits (a) and (c) but one forward- and one reverse-biased in circuit (b), so the drops are equal only when both share the same bias state.
why subtopic 2Circuit (b) joins a PN and an NP junction in series, so one is reverse-biased and takes almost the whole drop, and ruling (b) out depends on that reverse-bias behaviour.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in
  1. Circuit (a) only
  2. Circuit (b) only
  3. Circuit (c) only
  4. Both circuits (a) and (c)
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
  1. Potential drops across the p-n junctions will be same if either both junctions are forward biased or both junction are reverse biased.
  2. In figure (a) and (c), both junctions are forward biased therefore both have same potential.
  3. In figure (b) first junction is forward biased and second junction is reverse biased, so both junctions have different potential difference.

→ the working concludes: option 4

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
  1. In circuit (a) both junctions are oriented P→ N in series, so the same current flows through both with the same bias; identical junctions give V1 = V2.
  2. In circuit (b) one junction is P→ N and the other N→ P, so one is forward biased and the other reverse biased; Vforward ≪ Vreverse, so the drops are unequal.
  3. In circuit (c) both junctions are oriented N→ P in series, so both have the same bias and V1 = V2.
  4. Equal drops occur in (a) and (c), which is option 4.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
44 highagree
difficultymedium · 3 steps
stepsRead each circuit to find the orientation of the two series p-n junctions relative to the cell, deciding whether each is forward or reverse biased → Recognise that when both junctions in series have the same bias (both forward or both reverse) and are identical, the same current flows through them and the voltage divides equally → Recognise that when one is forward and the other reverse biased, the reverse-biased junction takes nearly all the voltage, so the drops are unequal, and pick the circuits with matching orientations
why it is trickyThe work is a bias reading of six junctions across three circuits followed by applying series-current reasoning to decide when the two drops are equal, including the case where both are reverse biased.
the catchSingle-circuit options (a) only and (c) only are the result of assuming drops are equal only when both junctions conduct, overlooking that two identical reverse-biased junctions also share the voltage equally.

why this chapterThe answer +5 D comes from the lens maker formula 1/f = (n-1)(1/R1 - 1/R2) with n = 1.5 and R = 20 cm, followed by P = 1/f, both taught in Ray Optics.
subtopic 1Lens Maker Formula

printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A biconvex lens has radii of curvature, 20 cm each. If the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5, the power of the lens is
  1. +2 D
  2. +20 D
  3. +5 D
  4. Infinity
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (3)
  1. Power of lens is given by
  2. P = 1f(m)
  3. 1f = (μ - 1)(1R1 - 1R2)
  4. 1f = {32 - 1}(120 + 120)
  5. f = 20 cm
  6. P = 120 × 10-2
  7. = 5 D

→ the working concludes: option 3

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 3 · high
  1. For a biconvex lens, R1 = +20 cm and R2 = -20 cm.
  2. 1f = (μ - 1)(1R1 - 1R2) = (1.5 - 1)(120 + 120) cm-1.
  3. 1f = 0.5 × 220 = 120 cm-1, so f = 20 cm = 0.2 m.
  4. P = 1f = 10.2 m = +5 D, which is option 3.

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · medium
  1. In a Schottky defect, equal numbers of cations and anions are missing, so the ionic solid stays electrically neutral even though some cations are missing: (A) is correct.
  2. In a Frenkel defect, a cation leaves its lattice site and occupies an interstitial site; the charge is unchanged, so neutrality is maintained: (R) is correct.
  3. In a Frenkel defect no cation is lost from the crystal, so (R) does not explain why a solid with missing cations is neutral: (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Given below are two statements
Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.

Statement IThe acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.

  2. Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
  3. Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
  4. Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (3)
  1. Nitro group has electron withdrawing tendency. It can withdraw electrons both by -I effect and -R effect. Thus the acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol.
  2. Nitro group present at o- and p-positions will have strong -R effect while nitro group present at m-position will influence only -I effect hence acidity or o/p isomer will be more meta isomer.

→ the working concludes: option 3

  2. Statement II: the -R effect works only from the ortho and para positions, and o-nitrophenol has intramolecular H-bonding, so the acidity order is p > o > m (pKa ≈ 7.1, 7.2, 8.3). The acidities are not the same, so Statement II is false.
  3. I is correct and II is incorrect, which is option 3.

At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu2+ / Cu, Zn2+ / Zn, Fe2+ / Fe and Ag+ / Ag are 0.34 V, -0.76 V, -0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur?
  1. CuSO4(aq) + Zn(s) → ZnSO4(aq) + Cu(s)
  2. CuSO4(aq) + Fe(s) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s)
  3. FeSO4(aq) + Zn(s) → ZnSO4(aq) + Fe(s)
  4. 2CuSO4(aq) + 2Ag(s) → 2Cu(s) + Ag2SO4(aq)

  1. For a reaction to be spontaneous, Eocell must be positive.
  2. For, FeSO4(aq) + Zn(s) → ZnSO4(aq) + Fe(s)
  3. Eocell = Eocathode - Eoanode
  4. = -0.44 V - (-0.76 V)
  5. = 0.32 V
  6. For, 2CuSO4(aq) + 2Ag(s) → 2Cu(s) + Ag2SO4(aq)
  7. Eocell = 0.34 V - 0.80 V
  8. = -0.46 V
  9. For, CuSO4(aq) + Zn(s) → ZnSO4(aq) + Cu(s)
  10. Eocell = 0.34 V - (-0.76 V)
  11. = 1.1 V
  12. For, CuSO4(aq) + Fe(s) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s)
  13. Eocell = 0.80 V - (-0.44 V)
  14. = 1.24 V

→ the working concludes: option 4

  2. Flocculating power of cation increases with increases in charge on cation of electrolyte in case of negatively charge colloid, hence order is

Given below are half cell reactions:
MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- → Mn2+ + 4H2O,
E°Mn2+/MnO4- = -1.510 V
12O2 + 2H+ + 2e- → H2O,
E°O2/H2O = +1.223 V
Will the permanganate ion, MnO4- liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
  1. Yes, because E°cell = +0.287 V
  2. No, because E°cell = -0.287 V
  3. Yes, because E°cell = +2.733 V
  4. No, because E°cell = -2.733 V
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (1)
  1. MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- ⟶ Mn2+ + 4H2O    …(i)
  2. E°MnO4-/Mn2+ = -E°Mn2+/MnO4- = 1.51 V
  3. H2O ⟶ 12O2 + 2H+ + 2e-    …(ii)
  4. E°O2/H2O = 1.223 V
  5. Using 2 × (i) + 5 × (ii), net cell reactions is
  6. 2MnO4- + 6H+ ⟶ 2Mn2+ + 52O2 + 3H2O
  7. E°cell = E°C - E°A = E°MnO4-/Mn2+ - E°O2/H2O = 1.51 - 1.223 = 0.287 V
  8. Since E°cell > 0, therefore net cell reaction is spontaneous and so MnO4- liberate O2 from H2O in presence of an acid.

→ the working concludes: option 1

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 1 · high
  1. The given E°Mn2+/MnO4- = -1.510 V is an oxidation potential, so E°MnO4-/Mn2+ = +1.510 V.
  2. Permanganate is reduced (cathode) and water is oxidised to O2 (anode).
  3. E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 1.510 - 1.223 = +0.287 V.
  4. E°cell > 0, so the reaction is spontaneous: yes, O2 is liberated, which is option 1.

    Which of the following statements are true for spermatogenesis but do not hold true for Oogenesis? Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
    (a)It results in the formation of haploid gametes
    (b)Differentiation of gamete occurs after the completion of meiosis
    (c)Meiosis occurs continuously in a mitotically dividing stem cell population
    (d)It is controlled by the Luteinising hormone (LH) and Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) secreted by the anterior pituitary
    (e)It is initiated at puberty

    2. (b) and (c) only
    3. (b), (d) and (e) only
    4. (b), (c) and (e) only
    The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
    1. Option (4) is the correct answer.
    2. In both, spermatogenesis and oogenesis haploid gametes are formed. So (a) is true for both.
    3. The spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa (sperms) by the process called spermiogenesis. Hence, (b) is true for spermatogenesis only.
    4. Spermatogenesis and oogenesis both are controlled by LH and FSH secreted by the anterior pituitary. Hence (d) is true for both.
    5. Spermatogenesis is a continuous process that begins at puberty. So (e) is true for spermatogenesis. Oogenesis on the other hand begins during embryonic development of the female.

    printed solution, as in the booklet
    Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
    1. (a) Both spermatogenesis and oogenesis form haploid gametes, so (a) is not exclusive to spermatogenesis.
    2. (b) Spermatids differentiate into sperms (spermiogenesis) after meiosis is complete; in oogenesis meiosis II finishes only after sperm entry, so (b) applies to spermatogenesis only.
    3. (c) Spermatogonia form a mitotically dividing stem-cell population that keeps entering meiosis; oogonia stop multiplying before birth, so (c) applies to spermatogenesis only.
    4. (d) Both processes are regulated by pituitary LH and FSH, so (d) is not exclusive.
    5. (e) Spermatogenesis begins at puberty, whereas oogenesis begins during foetal development, so (e) applies to spermatogenesis only.
    6. Hence (b), (c) and (e) only, which is option 4.

    In an E. Coli strain i gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?

    The publisher's solutionprinted answer (3)
    1. As the product of ‘i’ gene binds with the operator region and blocks the transcription and translation of z, y and a genes.
    2. It’s product is prevented from binding to the operator by attaching it with the inducer.
    3. As the inducer can now no more capable of binding with the repressor, thus, in all the cases, operator always gets attached with the repressor thereby preventing the transcription and transmission of z, y and a.

    3. The bound repressor blocks RNA polymerase, so z, y, a are not transcribed and therefore not translated, which is option 3.

    Which one of the following statements is correct?
    1. The atrio-ventricular node (AVN) generates an action potential to stimulate atrial contraction

    4. Increased ventricular pressure causes closing of the semilunar valves.
    The publisher's solutionprinted answer (3)
    1. Option (3) is the correct answer because during joint diastole, blood moves freely from atrium to ventricle as atrioventricular valve remain open during joint diastole.
    2. Option (4) is incorrect because decrease in ventricular pressure, during ventricular diastole closes semilunar valves to produce ‘dub’ heart sound.
    3. Option (1) is incorrect because SA node generates action potential to stimulate atrial contraction.

    2. Option 2 is false: the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are already open during joint diastole; atrial systole only adds about 30% more blood.
    3. Option 4 is false: increased ventricular pressure closes the AV valves and opens the semilunar valves; semilunar valves close when ventricular pressure falls below arterial pressure.
    4. Option 3 is true: during joint diastole the AV valves are open, so blood moves freely from atria into ventricles, giving option 3.

    The recombination frequency between the genes a & c is 5%, b & c is 15%, b & d is 9%, a & b is 20%, c & d is 24% and a & d is 29%. What will be the sequence of these genes on a linear chromosome?
    1. a, d, b, c

    3. a, b, c, d

    Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
    1. Recombination frequency is proportional to map distance, so the farthest pair a–d (29%) are the two ends.
    2. a–c = 5% is smallest from a, so c lies next to a: a, c, …
    3. c–b = 15% places b after c: a–b = 5 + 15 = 20%, matching the given value.
    4. b–d = 9% places d last: c–d = 15 + 9 = 24% and a–d = 5 + 15 + 9 = 29%, both matching.
    5. The order is a, c, b, d, which is option 4.
